Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our security team needs a short written confirmation on two points before we proceed with procurement: 1) Does Redwood use customer-provided content (API payloads, uploaded files, logs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve public or private models? 2) Can you describe the exact retention windows for customer content across runtime caches, logs, backups, and any analytics pipelines, and confirm whether data originating in EU regions remains in-region?

We're under a strict regulatory mandate and need a succinct statement we can attach to our risk review (preferably with an appendix outlining retention timelines and deletion mechanics). If there's a formal one-page attestation or playbook you can share, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a reply by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Best,
Emma Jenkins
Head of Cloud Security
ClearBank

Hi Emma — I’m Dev on Redwood Security. Below is the formal wording you can use for your risk review, followed by a concise retention and deletion appendix. I’ve attached an editable one-page attestation (PDF) and the longer playbook for your auditors.

Official statement (use as-is):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided content from hosted API requests, dedicated capacity, or private deployments to train or otherwise improve our public or internal models. Customer content is processed solely to fulfill the requested inference and associated platform operations unless a separate contractual clause explicitly permits model training."

Retention and deletion appendix (summary):
- Runtime ephemeral caches: KV caches and prefix caches are in-memory or on-device and are automatically evicted within 24 hours by default unless the customer enables a longer TTL via configuration. For EU-hosted customers, cache shards remain in-region.
- Request logs (for routing/observability): retained 30 days by default; can be reduced to 7 days via account config in the Console. Logs stored for analytics are pseudonymized and access-controlled.
- Backups and snapshots: encrypted backups are retained up to 90 days; customers may request immediate deletion, subject to restoration windows.
- Audit trails & billing records: retention is 1 year by default for operational compliance; exportable on request.
- Deleted-data workflow: customer-initiated deletion requests are actioned within 7 business days for primary runtime stores; residual copies in encrypted backups are scheduled for secure deletion within 90 days. We provide a deletion certificate on request.
- Private/on-prem deployments: data handling is entirely customer-controlled; Redwood's control plane does not ingest customer content in air-gapped setups unless explicitly configured for managed services.

Exceptions and clarifications:
- Aggregated, non-identifying telemetry used to monitor service health may be retained longer but is not tied to customer content for model training.
- If a customer signs an explicit agreement to allow use for model improvement (rare, opt-in), that clause will be documented and limited to specific datasets and duration; we do not take customer content for training under standard T&Cs.

Evidence and artifacts attached: redwood-nontraining-statement.pdf (signed template), data-deletion-playbook-2028.docx, SOC2_A3_redacted.pdf. We can generate a customer-specific attestation with ClearBank letterhead if required.

Let me know if you want any of the timelines tightened or a version that references your internal control IDs.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
